verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents bi-directional sync, a two-way connection between a ReadMe project and a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket repository, so teammates writing in the ReadMe web app and developers working in Git share one source of truth. It also documents an in-app editor with a formatting toolbar, multiplayer editing, and branches and reviews for approval. However, the evidence never explicitly presents the editor as a visual/WYSIWYG tool for non-technical users, and it does not detail how web edits become commits or how conflicts are resolved. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a WYSIWYG editor aimed at non-technical editors, detail on how web edits are committed to the repo and how sync conflicts are handled, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a technical writer, non-technical teammates can edit docs in a visual web editor without touching git, and their changes flow into the same source of truth

citations.quote: Bi-directional sync creates a two-way connection between your ReadMe project and a GitHub or GitLab repository.
Write in your preferred environment whether that's ReadMe or your local development setup.
Manage API definitions in Git while your team writes docs in ReadMe
When you select text, a prompt field appears in the formatting toolbar where you can type plain-language instructions and let the Agent apply the edits.
